screens.name: Standard & Auto-Reversing Journal Entries
screens.purpose: Record non-invoice transactions: month-end expense accruals, reclassifications, sweep entries, and intercompany allocations.
whyRecordsAreHere: Adjustments required to comply with US GAAP matching principles and correct site-team coding errors.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Journal Type
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Standard, Auto-Reversing, Accrual, Recurring.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Effective Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Must be within target open period (e.g. 08/31/2026).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Reversal Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Day 1 of subsequent month (e.g. 09/01/2026).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Description & Reference
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Audit trail mandatory explanation.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Draft entry with balanced Debits and Credits (Total Debits == Total Credits).
2. For month-end accruals (utilities, marketing, payroll), select 'Auto-Reverse' on Day 1 of next month.
3. Attach Excel calculation support and third-party backup (e.g., utility rate bills, payroll summary).
4. Post or submit for Onshore Reviewer approval depending on property authority policies.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Directly updates GL account balances and reflects immediately on the Trial Balance.
screens.whatHappensNext: If auto-reversing, RealPage system job automatically creates offsetting reversal entry on the 1st of next month.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Journal Entry (or Journal Entry Batch) > Add; tick 'Auto Reverse' and set the reversal period for accruals; post via Find Batch > Post.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf, Pages 256-265 (Adding a Journal Entry); Pages 298-299 (Reversing a Journal Entry)
screens.proTips: Always include the calculation formula and month in the line-item description (e.g., 'Aug 2026 Utility Accrual - 5 unbilled days').

screens.name: Duplicate Journal Entry (Same Book or Other Books)
screens.purpose: Clone an existing complex multi-line journal entry into the current journal or a different book (Accrual, Tax, Provisional, User-Defined) without re-keying account numbers, cost centers, and descriptions.
whyRecordsAreHere: Accountants execute recurring monthly journal entries (mortgage interest, utilities, management fee accruals, billbacks) where only dates or amounts change.
Allows testing entry impact: copy an entry into a Provisional/User-Defined book first to review financial statement impact before recording to the main Accrual book.
Eliminates manual data entry errors and transposition mistakes on multi-line reclassifications.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Duplicate Button
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Located on the top action toolbar when viewing a transaction or checking transactions in the list.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Duplicate To Box
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Dialog that opens to specify the destination Book (Accrual, GAAP, Tax, User-Defined) and Journal.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Date Selection
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Choose whether to use the original entry date or specify a new replacement target period date.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: New Transaction ID
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: System automatically assigns a unique sequential ID while copying all distribution lines.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Navigate to General Ledger > All > Journal Entry > View Transactions.
2. Locate the prior month journal entry to copy; click View or select its check box in the list.
3. Click the Duplicate button on the top action bar.
4. In the Duplicate To pop-up dialog, select target Book (e.g. Accrual) and Journal.
5. In Date section, choose Specify Date and input current month-end date (e.g. 08/31/2026).
6. Click OK; RealPage opens the cloned entry with a new Transaction ID.
7. Edit distribution dollar amounts and line descriptions to reflect current month support.
8. Verify Debits equal Credits, then click Post (or Save as Draft).
screens.glAccountingImpact: Cloned entry posts with new Transaction ID: Debits selected Expense/Asset GLs and Credits matching Liability/Equity GLs. Zero net imbalance allowed.
screens.whatHappensNext: New journal entry posts to the General Ledger and Trial Balance. Reflected on the monthly GL Detail Report and Comparative Income Statement.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Journal Entry > Find Batch > open the JE > 'Copy' function (creates an unposted copy you re-date and post); cross-book copies are re-keyed with the target Book selected.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf, Pages 296-297 and 404-406 (Duplicating Journal Entries to Other Books)
screens.proTips: RealPage does NOT check for duplicate journal entries during imports or copying (as stated on page 18 of the Importing Data guide). Always verify the Transaction ID and description to prevent accidentally posting the exact same entry twice!

screens.name: Duplicate a Prepaid Journal Entry
screens.purpose: Duplicate an existing prepaid amortization schedule to create a new recurring schedule for renewed policies or newly capitalized multi-month prepaid expenses.
whyRecordsAreHere: Annual insurance renewals, software subscriptions, or service contracts require setting up a new 12-month amortization schedule identical in structure to the expiring contract.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Duplicate Button
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Appears when viewing or editing an existing prepaid record in General Ledger > Periodic Tasks > Prepaids.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Asset & Expense Accounts
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Prepaid Asset (1200-00) and Target Expense (6300-00).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Amortization Term
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Number of months and start date.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Navigate to General Ledger > Periodic Tasks > Prepaids.
2. Locate the expiring or template prepaid record; click Edit.
3. Click the Duplicate button on the header toolbar.
4. System copies all values into a new record with a new unique schedule ID.
5. Update total premium/contract cost, start date, and number of amortization months.
6. Click Save to activate the automated monthly amortization batch.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Monthly auto-batch posts: DR 6300-00 Insurance Expense / CR 1200-00 Prepaid Insurance Asset.
screens.whatHappensNext: Schedule activates in the Pre-AME monthly recurring journal queue. Amortizes asset balance to $0 over term.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Recurring Journal Entry > open the prior amortization schedule > Copy, then update amount, start/end period and prepaid account.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf, Pages 492-493 (Duplicating a Prepaid Journal Entry)
screens.proTips: Check unamortized balance on the old schedule before activating the new duplicate to prevent overlapping double amortization.

screens.name: Recurring Amortization Schedules
screens.purpose: Automate monthly expensing of multi-month prepaid items (prepaid insurance, property software licenses, upfront loan costs).
whyRecordsAreHere: Large upfront payments must be capitalized as assets and systematically amortized over policy/loan term.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Asset Account
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: e.g., 1200-00 Prepaid Insurance.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Expense Account
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: e.g., 6300-00 Insurance Expense.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Term & Frequency
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: 12 months, monthly post on the 1st or last day.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Set up schedule when the annual invoice is paid.
2. Verify monthly amortization amount = Total Policy Cost / Total Policy Months.
3. Run monthly recurring journal batch during Pre-AME phase.
4. Check ending balance in Prepaid Asset on Balance Sheet agrees with unexpired policy period.
screens.glAccountingImpact: DR 6300-00 (Insurance Expense) / CR 1200-00 (Prepaid Insurance Asset).
screens.whatHappensNext: Prepaid asset balance amortizes down to zero over policy life; monthly expense stabilizes on the Income Statement.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Recurring Journal Entry (monthly DR expense / CR prepaid for the policy term) or the Payables 'Amortize' option on the payable line.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf, Pages 479-491 (Prepaids: Adding a Prepaid Journal Entry, Viewing the Prepaid Schedule)
screens.proTips: When an insurance policy is cancelled or renewed mid-term, adjust the schedule immediately to prevent negative prepaid balances.

screens.name: Trial Balance & GL Detail Inquiry
screens.purpose: Inspect debit and credit balances for every single chart of accounts line to verify ledger equilibrium and audit line movements.
whyRecordsAreHere: The bedrock report of property accounting. If Trial Balance is out of balance, financial statements cannot be issued.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Period & Date Range
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Month-to-date, Quarter-to-date, Year-to-date.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Zero Balance Accounts
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Toggle to exclude inactive accounts for clarity.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Run Trial Balance immediately after posting month-end journals.
2. Verify Total Debits == Total Credits (Variance == $0.00).
3. Check for abnormal balances: debit balances in liabilities/revenues, or credit balances in assets/expenses.
4. Drill down into transaction details for any unexpected or unmapped account balances.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Validates integrity of the complete double-entry bookkeeping ledger.
screens.whatHappensNext: Forms the basis for the Balance Sheet and Income Statement in the preliminary AME package.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Analytics > Financial Analytics > Trial Balance (select Book: Accrual/Cash, property list and period) and GL Detail (Ledger) report for drill-down.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.pdf, Pages 47-58 (Trial Balance Report); Pages 67-77 (General Ledger Report)
screens.proTips: Always check GL Account 1099 (Cash Clearing) and GL 2099 (AP Clearing)—both MUST be $0.00 at month-end.

screens.name: Invoice Exception Queue
screens.purpose: Resolve invoices that the RealPage Invoice Processing (Full Service) team could not complete and returned to the property/accounting team with exception messages. The Invoice exception button near the top of the page shows the number of waiting invoices; each item must be answered (comment/exception message), voided, or routed back to the team (Route to Pending QC) so it can be keyed, approved and paid on time.
whyRecordsAreHere: The Invoice Processing team needs clarification to process the invoice accurately (e.g., unknown or inactive vendor, unclear property/location, missing or mismatched PO, unreadable image, possible duplicate).
The invoice belongs to a vendor that is not yet set up or is on hold (missing W-9/COI, bank details pending verification).
Coding questions: capital vs. operating, which property/unit, or service period needed for accrual cut-off.
The document is not a payable invoice (statement, quote, past-due notice) and should be voided.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Invoice exception button
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Appears near the top of the page with a count when the Invoice Processing team sends invoices to the queue; opens the Invoice exception queue page.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Invoice OID
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Link that opens the invoice so you can review the image and details.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Exception messages / comment box
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Select a standard exception message (type part of the text to filter) or enter free-form text explaining how to process the invoice.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Add Comment
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Adds the selected messages to the invoice history with date, user ID, action comment and description.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Save / Void / Route to Pending QC
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Save keeps the invoice in the queue; Void voids it (confirm twice); Route to Pending QC sends it back to the team for final processing and removes it from the queue.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Click the Invoice exception button at the top of the page to open the Invoice exception queue.
2. Sort by oldest date and highest amount; open each invoice via the Invoice OID link and review the image and the team's exception message.
3. Resolve the root cause: ask the site to confirm the property/unit or service period, have vendor setup completed (W-9, COI, remit/ACH verified by call-back), or obtain the PO/receipt.
4. In the comment box select the matching exception message(s) or type clear instructions (property, GL account, PO number), then click Add Comment.
5. Choose the action: Save (still waiting), Void (not a payable invoice / duplicate), or Route to Pending QC to send it back to the Invoice Processing team.
6. Control check: if an exception is still open at month-end, accrue the expense (DR expense / CR 2020 Accrued Expenses) so the period is not understated.
screens.glAccountingImpact: No GL entries while the invoice sits in the exception queue. When processed and approved: DR 6xxx Operating Expense (or capital/prepaid account) / CR 2010 Accounts Payable. Voiding here creates no entry because the invoice never posted.
screens.whatHappensNext: Routed invoices go to Pending QC with the Invoice Processing team, then into the A/P approval workflow (Approval Workbench) and payment selection; voided items leave the queue.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan > Invoice Register / Workflow 'Exception' (or 'Hold') step where invoices needing information are reassigned to the property with notes before approval.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf, Pages 322-327 (Invoice Exception Queue, Resolving an Exception Invoice); RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf, Pages 504-509
screens.proTips: Always sort by Age in Days and dollar amount. Invoices over 30 days in exception severely hurt vendor credit terms and prompt warning flags during onshore audits.

screens.name: Manage Invoices & Batch Entry
screens.purpose: Central dashboard to search, view, edit, reclassify, or track the real-time workflow status of all property vendor invoices.
whyRecordsAreHere: Every invoice scanned, imported via EDI, or manually entered by site staff or offshore processing teams resides here.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Status Filter
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Pending Approval, Approved, Paid, Exception, Void, In Process.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Invoice Date Range
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Crucial for isolating invoices by target accounting period.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Vendor Search
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Look up by vendor trade name or RealPage vendor ID.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Use Status = 'Approved' to forecast cash disbursements for the weekly payment run.
2. Verify invoice image quality and ensure sales tax is coded to appropriate tax GL or operational line.
3. Check that invoices are not backdated into closed accounting periods without prior controller permission.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Approved invoices post to the AP Subledger and immediately reflect on the Trial Balance and General Ledger (DR Expense / CR AP 2000-00).
screens.whatHappensNext: Invoices appear on the Cash Requirements Report and are selected for check or ACH payment during the weekly AP payment run.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable (Find/Payable Batch) and PAYscan > Invoice Register for scanned invoices with workflow status.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf, Pages 265-289 (A/P Invoices, Viewing the A/P Invoices List, Exporting the A/P Invoices List)
screens.proTips: Use the 'Batch ID' search when reconciling vendor statements to see all invoices submitted in a single upload.

screens.name: Select Invoices for Payment (Check Run)
screens.purpose: Select approved vendor bills and resident security deposit refunds to prepare physical check batches, ACH files, or wire transfers.
whyRecordsAreHere: Invoices that have completed all approval tiers (1st, 2nd, and Accounting) and reached their due date appear in the eligible payment pool.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Payment Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: The check or ACH value date posted to the general ledger.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Bank Account
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Operating Account from which funds will be disbursed.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Due Date Cutoff
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Filters invoices due on or before specified calendar date.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Check morning collected cash balance in operating account to establish total payment limit.
2. Select eligible invoices; generate the 'Cash Requirements Summary' report for review.
3. Exclude disputed invoices or vendors with open credit memos.
4. Generate payment batch and route to Onshore Signer for release authorization.
screens.glAccountingImpact: DR 2000-00 (Accounts Payable Subledger) / CR 1010-00 (Operating Cash Account).
screens.whatHappensNext: Payment batch creates checks or NACHA file. Disbursed checks appear on the Bank Reconciliation Outstanding Checks list.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Processing > Create Checks (Auto Pay by bank, property list, due date) > Print Checks; ACH via Payables > EFT.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf, Pages 745-778 (Paying A/P Invoices); Pages 1042-1049 (Check Runs, Adding a Check Run)
screens.proTips: Always ensure credit memos are selected alongside vendor invoices to avoid overpaying vendors.

screens.name: Void & Re-issue Payments
screens.purpose: Void lost, expired, returned, or erroneous vendor checks and re-issue or restore the underlying invoice.
whyRecordsAreHere: Checks returned as undeliverable, stale-dated (>90 days), or lost in transit by vendors or past residents.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Void Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Must be within the current open accounting period; never backdate into closed periods.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Void Reason
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Required audit note (e.g., Stale Dated, Wrong Payee Name, Stop Payment Placed).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Re-issue Option
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Choose whether to immediately generate a new check or restore invoice to unpaid status.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Verify stop-payment confirmation is active in bank portal.
2. Enter check number in RealPage Manage Payments and select 'Void'.
3. Set void date to current month; attach stop-payment confirmation letter.
4. Confirm book cash balance is credited and bank rec outstanding list updates.
screens.glAccountingImpact: DR 1010-00 (Operating Cash) / CR 2000-00 (Accounts Payable Subledger).
screens.whatHappensNext: Cleared from Bank Rec outstanding check schedule. If re-issued, a new check number is generated on the next AP check run.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check > Find > Void Check (choose void date/post month; option to also void the payable), then re-pay through Check Processing.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf, Pages 1025-1038 (Voiding a Check); Page 1053 (Voiding a Check in a Check Run)
screens.proTips: If voiding resident refund checks, check local state unclaimed property (escheatment) laws if older than 180 days.

screens.name: Invoice Exception Report
screens.purpose: Executive report listing all invoices currently blocked from payment, grouped by exception reason and property.
whyRecordsAreHere: Used by accountants, PMs, and onshore managers during weekly AP reviews to ensure no critical bills are stalled.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Property Selection
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Run by individual asset or portfolio-wide.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Aging Buckets
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: 0-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, 90+ days.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Exception Category
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: PO Variance, ROG, Compliance, GL Mismatch.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Run every Monday morning before the weekly team calls.
2. Highlight utility invoices, contractor draw bills, and tax assessments in exception.
3. Assign action items to site team members with explicit resolution deadlines.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Informational report; highlights potential unrecorded liabilities needing month-end accrual.
screens.whatHappensNext: Site team resolves exceptions; invoices move to approval queue. If unresolved at month-end, accountant records unbilled invoice accrual.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan > Invoice Register filtered by workflow step 'Exception/Hold' and exported to Excel for month-end accrual review.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf, Page 322 (Invoice Exception Queue); RP Financial Suite Spend Management QS.pdf, Page 3 (Using the Full Service Invoice Exception Queue)
screens.proTips: If an invoice remains in exception past month-end cutoff, you MUST book an unbilled invoice accrual (DR Expense / CR Accrued Expenses).

screens.name: Vendor Aging & Trial Balance
screens.purpose: Displays all unpaid vendor invoices categorized into 30, 60, 90, and 120+ day aging columns.
whyRecordsAreHere: Essential month-end schedule to tie out the AP subledger to the General Ledger AP control account.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: As of Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Always set to last calendar day of the accounting month.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Summary vs Detail
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Detail view shows individual invoice numbers and dates.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Run as of month-end date.
2. Verify total ending vendor aging ties exactly to GL Account 2000-00 (Accounts Payable).
3. Investigate any debit balances (vendor credit balances) and request refunds or offset against upcoming bills.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Total Vendor Aging must equal GL Account 2000-00 to the penny. Zero variance allowed.
screens.whatHappensNext: Schedule is signed off and included as Schedule 2 in the Monthly Operating Report (MOR) package for the asset manager.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Analytics > Payable Analytics > Aging (as of post month) compared with Financial Analytics > Trial Balance for the A/P control account.
screens.pdfManualSource: Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf, Pages 2-8 (Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Don't Match, Steps 1-5)
screens.proTips: Never close the AP subledger if Vendor Aging does not tie to GL 2000-00.

screens.name: Bank Reconciliation Workbench
screens.purpose: Reconcile property bank account statement balances against internal book general ledger cash balances.
whyRecordsAreHere: Mandatory internal control performed monthly for every bank account (Operating, Depository, Security Deposit, Escrow).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Statement Ending Balance
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Exact closing balance printed on the official bank statement.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Cutoff Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Statement period end date (e.g. 08/31/2026).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Difference to Balance
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Must equal exactly $0.00 before reconciliation can be saved/posted.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Enter statement ending balance and cutoff date from bank PDF.
2. Clear checks, ACH disbursements, and bank debits that match statement records.
3. Clear customer deposits and merchant settlement batches.
4. Post any unrecorded bank fees or interest directly from the reconciliation screen.
5. Confirm 'Difference to Balance' equals $0.00; generate and sign reconciliation package.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Interest Earned: DR 1010-00 / CR 7100-00 Interest Income. Bank Charges: DR 6850-00 / CR 1010-00 Cash.
screens.whatHappensNext: Signed bank rec report attaches to monthly MOR package for Onshore Reviewer and Lender inspection.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Bank Reconciliation (Advanced Bank Rec with BAI2 import/auto-match), Bank Rec Report and Outstanding Items report.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf, Pages 224-263 (Bank Reconciliation (New), Reconciling a Bank Account, Why Doesn't My Bank Reconciliation Balance Match the Bank Statement?)
screens.proTips: If there is a difference, check for duplicate cleared items or checks cleared for an amount different than written (bank encoding error).

screens.name: Sweep Entries & Inter-Account Transfers
screens.purpose: Record daily or monthly automated bank sweeps between depository accounts and main concentration/operating accounts.
whyRecordsAreHere: Properties use depository accounts for local resident check deposits, which banks sweep nightly into central concentration accounts.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Source Account
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Depository Account.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Destination Account
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Operating Account.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Transfer Amount & Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Must match bank sweep debit/credit exactly.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Pull daily bank statements for both Depository and Operating accounts.
2. Match the debit in Depository with the credit in Operating.
3. Post Transfer in RealPage Cash Management to mirror the sweep on company books.
4. Verify both accounts reflect balanced cash without double-counting.
screens.glAccountingImpact: DR 1010-00 (Operating Cash) / CR 1020-00 (Depository Cash). Zero net impact on Total Cash.
screens.whatHappensNext: Balances on Depository account return to zero, preventing false negative book balances.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: cash-to-cash transfer recorded via Financials > Journal Entry (DR destination cash / CR source cash) or intercompany Due To/Due From when entities differ.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf, Pages 95-105 (Funds Transfer, Adding a Funds Transfer, Reversing a Funds Transfer, Transferring Funds in Bulk)
screens.proTips: Sweeps that occur on the last day of the month often credit the receiving bank on the 1st of next month. Book as Deposit in Transit!

screens.name: Delinquency Aging Report
screens.purpose: Track past-due resident balances aged 30, 60, and 90+ days to calculate bad debt reserves and initiate legal notices.
whyRecordsAreHere: Residents who missed rent payments, failed to pay utility rebills, or incurred uncollected lease termination fees.
Moved-out residents with damage charges exceeding their security deposit.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Resident Status
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Current, Notice, Eviction, Moved Out.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Aging Columns
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Current, 30-59 days, 60-89 days, 90+ days.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Exclude Inactive
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Exclude residents whose accounts have been sent to third-party collections.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Run report on the 10th of the month and at month-end.
2. Apply ownership reserve policy (e.g. 50% for 60-89 days, 100% for 90+ days and all skipped/evicted units).
3. Compare total required allowance against current balance in GL 1150-00.
4. Post Bad Debt adjustment entry in the general ledger.
screens.glAccountingImpact: DR 6350-00 (Bad Debt Expense) / CR 1150-00 (Allowance for Doubtful Accounts).
screens.whatHappensNext: Delinquency schedule is sent to Property Manager and Asset Manager for eviction strategy; bad debt reflects on income statement.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Analytics > Receivable Analytics > Aging (Resident Aging / Delinquency report by property and aging bucket).
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting AR Reports User Guide.pdf, Pages 13-18 (Customer Aging Report, Customizing the Customer Aging Report); RP Accounting AR Setup User Guide.pdf, Page 31 (Configuring A/R Aging)
screens.proTips: Always ensure security deposits have been applied against past-due balances before computing the net delinquent amount.

screens.name: Rent Roll & GPR Tie-Out
screens.purpose: Reconcile the physical property rent roll with the general ledger revenue accounts (Gross Potential Rent, Vacancy, Concessions).
whyRecordsAreHere: Multifamily properties bill rent at 100% market rent (GPR) and record vacancies, employee discounts, and concessions as contra-revenue.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: As of Date
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Last day of the accounting month.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Summary Mode
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Displays total units, occupied units, leased units, and total market rent.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Generate month-end Rent Roll Summary in RealPage.
2. Extract: Total Market Rent, Vacancy Loss, Model Units, Employee Discounts, and Concessions.
3. Verify that Net Billed Rent equals Net Rental Income on the Income Statement.
4. Book monthly Gross Potential Rent (GPR) journal entry.
screens.glAccountingImpact: DR 5100-00 (Vacancy Loss) / DR 5150-00 (Concessions) / DR 1100-00 (Resident AR) / CR 5000-00 (Gross Potential Rent).
screens.whatHappensNext: Certified revenue schedule attaches to AME package; locks rental revenue from further alteration.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Residents > Rent Roll (Rent Roll with Lease Charges) and Analytics > Residential Analytics > Gross Potential Rent / Box Score reconciled to the GL rent accounts.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf, Pages 48 (Lost Rent Summary Report), 56-60 (Rent Roll Detail Report and Columns)
screens.proTips: Multiply total unit count by average market rent per unit to perform a quick sanity tie-out.

screens.name: Financial Close Dashboard & Subledger Lock
screens.purpose: Enforce strict accounting period cutoffs by locking subledgers sequentially to prevent unauthorized backdating.
whyRecordsAreHere: Audit requirement. Once AP, AR, and Cash are verified, they must be locked so site teams cannot post late entries.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Period
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Target accounting month/year (e.g. 08/2026).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Module Lock Status
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Open, Staged, Closed, Locked.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Lock AP Subledger on Day 3 of close after all vendor invoices are entered.
2. Lock AR Subledger on Day 4 after rent roll and delinquency are balanced.
3. Lock Cash Management after bank reconciliations tie to $0.00.
4. Execute GL close diagnostic report to verify zero unposted batches.
5. Lock General Ledger and request Controller sign-off.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Locks Retained Earnings and Net Operating Income (NOI) against any further postings.
screens.whatHappensNext: Period is permanently locked. Any subsequent adjustments must be booked in the following accounting month.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Financials > Closing > Post Month (AP/AR post month by property) and Year End Close; close tasks tracked via Task Runner/workflow checklists or a third-party close tool.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Financial Suite Financial Close Management User Guide.pdf, Pages 38-41 (Close Checklist Page), 67-70 (Console); RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf, Pages 54-55 (Closing Books from the G/L Workbench)
screens.proTips: Never unlock a closed subledger without written authorization from the Financial Controller.

jobcost.title: Mastery Playbook — Curated CapEx & Reserve Workflows

screens.name: Replacement Reserve Draw Compiler
screens.purpose: Compile paid capital invoices, proof of payment (cleared checks), and contractor lien waivers to request reimbursement from mortgage lender reserves.
whyRecordsAreHere: Multifamily owners escrow funds monthly with lenders for major capital upgrades (roofs, HVAC, asphalt, unit turns).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Job Code / Project ID
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Unique capital improvement project number.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Eligible Invoices
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Invoices meeting capital threshold (> $1,000 / life > 1 year).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Lien Waiver Status
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Verified unconditional final lien waiver attached.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Gather paid vendor invoices and cancelled checks for completed capital projects.
2. Verify each invoice has an approved contractor lien waiver.
3. Prepare official Lender Draw Request Form categorized by approved escrow lines.
4. Submit draw package to Onshore Reviewer and Lender Inspector.
5. Upon receipt of wire from lender: post deposit to operating cash and reduce reserve receivable.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Wire received: DR 1010-00 (Operating Cash) / CR 1230-00 (Replacement Reserve Escrow / Due from Lender).
screens.whatHappensNext: Lender wire replenishes operating bank cash for funds spent on capital projects.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Job Cost > Draw (reserve-funded jobs) to build the draw request and Draw Report; lender reimbursement recorded via Receivables/Journal Entry against the reserve escrow account.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Financial Suite Replacement Reserves User Guide.pdf, Pages 17-18 (Adding a Replacement Reserve Draw); RP Financial Suite Job Cost & Reserves User Guide.pdf, Pages 64-68
screens.proTips: Lenders immediately reject draw packages missing even a single contractor lien waiver—verify waivers before submitting.

fixed_assets.title: Mastery Playbook — Curated Fixed Asset Workflows

screens.name: Fixed Asset Register & Depreciation Posting
screens.purpose: Calculate and post monthly depreciation expense for buildings, building improvements, furniture, appliances, and land improvements.
whyRecordsAreHere: Capitalized assets lose economic value over time and must be depreciated under US GAAP straight-line rules.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Asset Class
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Building (27.5 yrs), Land Improvements (15 yrs), FF&E (5-7 yrs).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Depreciation Method
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Straight-line, Half-Year Convention.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Review monthly additions to verify they meet property capitalization threshold (typically > $1,000 or $2,500).
2. Execute monthly depreciation calculation batch in RealPage Fixed Assets.
3. Verify depreciation schedule ties to Balance Sheet Accumulated Depreciation contra-asset account.
4. Post depreciation journal entry.
screens.glAccountingImpact: DR 6900-00 (Depreciation Expense) / CR 1750-00 (Accumulated Depreciation).
screens.whatHappensNext: Depreciation expense posts below Net Operating Income (NOI); accumulated depreciation reduces net book value of property assets.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager Fixed Assets: Fixed Assets > Depreciation (Calculate/Post Depreciation by property and period) and the Asset Register / Depreciation Schedule reports.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Financial Suite Fixed Assets User Guide.pdf, Pages 55-60 (Post Depreciation, Depreciation Batches List, Posting Depreciation Journal Entries)
screens.proTips: Land is NEVER depreciated. Ensure land acquisition values are separated into non-depreciable asset account 1500-00.

screens.name: MOR (Monthly Operating Report) Compiler
screens.purpose: Compile the complete, standardized investor financial package (Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Cash Flow, Bank Recs, Rent Roll).
whyRecordsAreHere: Standard monthly deliverable delivered to property owners, institutional clients (Goldman Sachs, OSSO), and lenders.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Reporting Period
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Target month (e.g. August 2026).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Package Template
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Investor specific template (e.g. GS Standard, Magnolia Core).

accountantActionSOP: 1. Verify all AME tie-outs are complete and verified.
2. Run package generator in RealPage Reporting Portal.
3. Review compiled PDF for formatting, missing page numbers, or unattached schedules.
4. Verify Net Income agrees across Balance Sheet, Income Statement, and Cash Flow Statement.
5. Publish to SharePoint and submit to Onshore Reviewer.
screens.glAccountingImpact: Reflects finalized financial state; locks period upon distribution.
screens.whatHappensNext: Transmitted to asset managers, investors, and lenders for debt service and operational reviews.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Report Scheduler / Report Packets (Analytics > Report Packet) combining Financial Analytics, bank rec and aging reports into one monthly package.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf, Pages 410-421 (Report Groups List, Adding a Report Group, Running a Report Group On Demand, Scheduling a Report Group)
screens.proTips: Always check that the Bank Rec Summary schedule in the MOR matches the Balance Sheet Cash line to the exact penny.

screens.name: Budget Model Creation (Annual Operating Budget Build)
screens.purpose: Builds the next fiscal year's property operating budget as a Working Budget in Forecasting & Planning. You seed it from the current G/L budget or a prior working budget, pick the fiscal months and properties, then refine it account by account (grow-by %/$ calculations, itemization rows, payroll publishing). Nothing becomes the official budget until you publish it to a G/L budget that reports and budget checks use. In institutional multifamily this is the Q3/Q4 cycle: the property submits, the asset manager reviews and the owner approves, all before January 1.
whyRecordsAreHere: Owner/asset-manager calendar requires a draft operating budget per property (typically submitted Sept–Oct, approved by Dec 15).
New acquisition or lease-up property needs a first-year budget before the first owner report.
Budget seeded from the prior year's G/L budget and actuals so every revenue and expense account is carried forward.
Payroll plan (positions, wages, taxes, benefits) must be built separately and published into the working budget's payroll accounts.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Budget
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Unique name for the working budget (e.g. FY2027 Operating - Draft v1). Use a naming convention with fiscal year and version.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Creation method
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Create a new budget; Create a budget from working budget and reporting period range; or Create a budget from G/L budget and reporting period range (seed from the current year).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Source year / Create for year
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Year the seed data comes from and the fiscal year being budgeted.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Start fiscal month / End fiscal month
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Reporting periods that bound the budget (normally the 12 months of the fiscal year).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Accounts
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: All accounts, or Select account group to limit the budget to an account group (e.g. the owner reporting P&L group).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Property
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Multi-select of the properties (locations) the working budget covers.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Status
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Working (default) until published; changes to Published after Publish.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Grow by / Compute amount
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Account-level calculation that grows each period by a dollar amount or a percentage from a starting amount.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Confirm the chart of accounts and the owner's budget account group are current (Applications > General Ledger > Account Groups) before you create the budget.
2. Open Forecasting & Planning > All tab; in Periodic tasks click the Add (+) icon next to Working budgets.
3. Type the Budget name using the convention FY{year} Operating – {Property} – v1.
4. Choose Create a budget from G/L budget and reporting period range, then select the current-year G/L budget as the seed, the Source year, and the Create for year.
5. Set Start fiscal month and End fiscal month to the 12 fiscal periods of the budget year.
6. Select Accounts: pick the owner's reporting account group so only reportable P&L lines are budgeted.
7. Select the Property (or properties) and click Save; status shows Working.

8. Open Budget details and work each account: use Grow by % for inflation-driven lines (utilities +4%, insurance +12%), Amount for contract-driven lines, and itemization rows for multi-component lines (e.g. contract services).

9. Build revenue from the rent roll: GPR = units × market rent × 12, less loss-to-lease, vacancy (budgeted occupancy), concessions and bad debt; attach the revenue build worksheet as an account comment.
10. Build payroll in the Payroll workbench (positions, raises effective dates, taxes, benefits, workers comp) and publish the payroll to this working budget.
11. Export the working budget to Excel for asset-manager review; import the reviewed version back with Importing Data into a Working Budget.
12. Control check: total budgeted NOI must reconcile to the approved budget memo; budgeted units × months must match the rent roll unit count before submission.
screens.glAccountingImpact: No GL impact — a working budget is planning data stored outside the actual ledger. Only after it is published to a G/L budget does it feed budget-vs-actual (BVA) reports, dashboards and budget checks on purchase orders and A/P invoices.
screens.whatHappensNext: The draft goes to the asset manager or owner for review. Revisions are made in the same working budget, then it is published (Publishing a Working Budget) to the official G/L budget used by BVA reports, the Budget Report and the Prevent/Warn budget checks.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Budgeting & Forecasting / Forecast IQ budget workflow (property budget model with revenue, payroll and expense driver sheets), or Financials > Budget > Budget Import for spreadsheet-built budgets; approval via the budget workflow before posting to the budget book.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting Forecasting & Planning User Guide.pdf, Pages 168-171 (Working Budgets List, Adding a Working Budget), 181-195 (working budget account details, Calculating the Budget Increase), 215-216 (Copying Records from a Previous Year); RP Accounting Forecasting & Planning QS.pdf, Pages 1-2
screens.proTips: Seed from the current G/L budget, not from actuals only — actuals carry one-time items (insurance claims, legal settlements) that should not recur. Document every material assumption in the account comment; the asset manager's first question is always 'what drives this line?'.

screens.name: Budget Re-forecast & Revisions (Mid-Year Reforecast)
screens.purpose: Produces a mid-year reforecast (e.g. 6+6 or 9+3) or a formal budget revision without overwriting the approved original budget. You duplicate the approved working budget, advance year-to-date actuals into the elapsed months, re-project the remaining months, and publish the result to a separate G/L budget (e.g. FY2026 Reforecast Q2). That way BVA can compare actuals to both the original budget and the reforecast.
whyRecordsAreHere: Owner or asset manager requests a quarterly reforecast after material variances (insurance renewal, tax reassessment, occupancy shift).
Loan covenant or distribution planning needs a current full-year NOI projection.
An approved budget revision (e.g. added capital project or staffing change) must be tracked separately from the original budget.
Year-to-date actuals must replace budget in closed months so the full-year projection is accurate.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Duplicate
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Copies an existing working budget (all accounts, properties and itemizations) under a new name.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Advance Actuals
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Replaces budget amounts in elapsed periods with year-to-date actual G/L balances (Advancing Year-to-Date Actuals).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Compare with budget / actuals
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Workbench comparison of the working budget against another budget or actuals.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Publish to
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: G/L budget the reforecast is published as; use a distinct budget name so the original approved budget is preserved.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Property list (publish)
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Clear a property to exclude it from this publish while its reforecast is still in progress.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Publish history
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Shows each publish event of a working budget (who/when) for version audit.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Close the last month in scope (all accruals posted) so year-to-date actuals are final before reforecasting.
2. Open Forecasting & Planning > All > Working budgets, click View on the approved budget, then Duplicate it; name the copy FY{year} Reforecast Q{n}.
3. In the duplicate, open Advance Actuals and advance year-to-date actuals through the last closed month.
4. Re-project the remaining months account by account using Calculating the Budget Increase or itemization rows; record the reason in Adding a Comment to an Account's Budget Details.

5. Use Comparing the Working Budget with Another Budget or with Actuals in the workbench to review the reforecast against the original budget; explain every line that moves by more than the owner threshold.
6. Obtain asset-manager approval of the reforecast package (exported to Excel/PDF).
7. Publish the working budget to a NEW G/L budget name (never publish over the original approved budget).
8. Check the publish history and the Budgets list to confirm both the original budget and the reforecast exist.
9. Control check: reforecast full-year NOI = YTD actual NOI + remaining-months projected NOI; tie YTD actual NOI to the closed-period income statement.
screens.glAccountingImpact: No GL impact — reforecasts and revisions are budget data. Advancing actuals reads posted G/L balances but posts nothing; publishing creates or updates a G/L budget used only for reporting and budget checks.
screens.whatHappensNext: Owner reports can show Actual vs Original Budget and Actual vs Reforecast side by side. Budget checks and BVA use whichever budget is set as the reporting budget, so confirm with the controller before changing any default budget selection.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Forecast IQ reforecast (copy budget version, roll actuals into closed periods, re-project remaining periods) or Financials > Budget with a separate budget book/version (e.g. 'Reforecast') imported alongside the original budget.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting Forecasting & Planning User Guide.pdf, Pages 23-24 (Comparing the Working Budget), 174-180 (Publish History, Duplicating a Working Budget, Advance Actuals), 188-190 (Publishing a Working Budget), 195 (Adding a Comment)
screens.proTips: Never publish a reforecast over the approved budget. Institutional owners measure the property team against the original budget for bonuses and against the reforecast for cash planning, so both must survive.

screens.name: GL Budget Comparison (Budget vs Actual Review)
screens.purpose: Runs the monthly budget-vs-actual (BVA) review that institutional owners require: actual MTD/YTD against the published budget by account, with dollar and percentage variances. You use the Income Statement Budget Comparison financial report and the Budget Variance Analysis workflow to capture variance explanations. It is the core of the owner reporting package, alongside the T-12 and balance sheet.
whyRecordsAreHere: Month-end owner package requires BVA with written explanations for every line over the variance threshold.
Asset managers use BVA to challenge operating performance and approve reforecasts.
Variances often expose accounting errors (miscoding, missing accruals, double-posted invoices) before the package is released.
Budget Variance Analysis periods track which properties have completed their variance notes.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Reporting period
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Current Month / Year to Date (or custom reporting period) for MTD and YTD columns.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Budget
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: The published G/L budget to compare with (original or reforecast).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Reporting book
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Accrual (typical for owner reporting) vs Cash; include adjustment books when required.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Location / location group
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Property or portfolio; Include subs for child locations.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Variance columns
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Actual − Budget in dollars and percent; set the sign convention so favorable/unfavorable is clear for revenue vs expense.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Budget Variance Analysis notes
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Per-account explanations entered in the BVA period; can be excluded from reports.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Confirm the period is soft-closed (Phase 6 of the close): accruals, prepaids, depreciation and management fees are posted.
2. Open General Ledger > Reports > Financial Statements and run the Income Statement Budget Comparison for the property, selecting the published budget and Accrual book.
3. Export to Excel and flag every account where |variance| exceeds the owner threshold (for example ±10% AND ±$5,000; configure per owner).
4. Drill into each flagged account (click the amount → GL detail) to confirm the variance is operational, not a posting error; fix miscodes with reclass JEs before commenting.
5. Open General Ledger > Budget Variance Analysis > Periods, open the property's period and enter the variance note for each flagged account (cause, timing vs permanent, expected recovery).
6. Re-run the report after corrections and attach the final BVA with notes to the close work papers.
7. Control check: report total revenue, total expense and NOI must tie to the income statement and trial balance for the same period and book.
screens.glAccountingImpact: No GL impact — read-only comparison of posted actuals with budget amounts. If the review finds a miscode, the correcting reclass is a separate journal entry (e.g. DR 6110 Repairs & Maintenance / CR 6120 Turnover), which you can create from the Budget Variance Report (Creating a Journal Entry from a Budget Variance Report).
screens.whatHappensNext: Variance notes and the BVA report go into the monthly owner package. Recurring or permanent variances feed the next reforecast, and unexplained variances hold the package until resolved.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Analytics > Financial Analytics > Budget Comparison (Income Statement Budget Comparison / 12-Month Budget vs Actual) with variance commentary in the owner report package (Report Packet).
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf, Pages 623-645 (Budget Variance Analysis, Viewing Budget Variance Reports, Creating a Journal Entry from a Budget Variance Report); RP Accounting Forecasting & Planning User Guide.pdf, Pages 145-151 (Budget Report)
screens.proTips: Explain variances in operational terms ('3 unbudgeted HVAC compressor replacements, $7,450, one-time') and state whether they are timing or permanent. 'Over budget' is not an explanation, and owners reject it.

screens.name: Variance Threshold Locking (Budget Checks: Prevent / Warn)
screens.purpose: Configures spend control against the published budget: when an A/P invoice or purchase order would exceed the budgeted amount for its G/L account, RealPage either warns the user or prevents the transaction. The budget-check duration can be the current month or the current year. Combined with Approval Policy Manager budget checks, this locks spending to the approved budget and forces over-budget items through an escalated approval.
whyRecordsAreHere: Owner requires hard controls so property teams cannot commit spend beyond the approved budget without escalation.
Repeated unfavorable R&M or turnover variances call for Warn (or Prevent) at PO entry.
Approval policies need a budget-check step so over-budget invoices route to the regional manager or asset manager.
Emergency spend may require an authorized bypass, which must be restricted and auditable.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Enable preventing or warning (A/P invoice)
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Check box in A/P Invoice Approvals; choose Warn (message only) or Prevent (blocks saving/posting).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Enable preventing or warning (Purchase order)
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Same control applied to purchase orders so the check happens at commitment, before the vendor is engaged.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Default duration
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Current month (budget for the posting month) or Current year (annual budget for the account).

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Budget check in approvals
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Setting Up a Budget Check As Part of Approvals routes over-budget transactions to additional approvers.

keyFieldsAndFilters.name: Bypass permission
keyFieldsAndFilters.description: Bypassing Budget Checks / the Prevent or Warn setting, restricted to specific roles for emergencies.

accountantActionSOP: 1. Confirm the correct budget is published and designated for budget checks; the check compares against published budget amounts only.
2. Open Applications > Company > All tab > Approvals > Approval Configuration.
3. In A/P Invoice Approvals select 'Enable preventing or warning a user when adding an AP Invoice that exceeds the budget' and choose Warn or Prevent per owner policy.
4. In Purchase orders select the equivalent option so over-budget commitments are caught at PO entry.
5. In Budget check set Default duration: Current year for annual-controlled accounts, Current month for owners that manage to monthly budgets.
6. Click Save, then set up the budget check step in the approval policy (Setting Up a Budget Check As Part of Approvals) so over-budget items route to the asset manager.
7. Restrict the bypass permission to controller-level roles and review bypass usage monthly.
8. Test with a sample PO over budget in a test property to confirm the Warn/Prevent message and the approval routing.
9. Control check: document the threshold configuration and any owner-approved exceptions in the close binder; review it after every budget publish or reforecast.
screens.glAccountingImpact: No GL impact — configuration only. It controls whether over-budget A/P invoices and POs can be saved or posted. When they post, invoices still record DR 6xxx Operating Expense / CR 2010 Accounts Payable; the control affects authorization, not the entry.
screens.whatHappensNext: Over-budget transactions show a warning or are blocked at entry. Approval routing escalates them, and BVA variances shrink because unauthorized overruns are stopped before commitment.
screens.yardiEquivalent: Yardi Voyager: Procure to Pay / PAYscan budget checks (PO and invoice workflow 'Over Budget' step with Warn/Stop settings by GL account and period) configured in workflow setup.
screens.pdfManualSource: RP Accounting General Ledger User Guide.pdf, Pages 597-600 (Setting Up a Budget Check As Part of Approvals, Setting a System Action When a Transaction Exceeds the Budget, Bypassing Budget Checks); RP Accounting Forecasting & Planning User Guide.pdf, Pages 166-167; RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf, Pages 36-46
screens.proTips: Start with Warn for 1–2 months so site teams learn the control, then move chronic overrun accounts (R&M, turnover, contract services) to Prevent. Keep utilities and taxes on Warn; you cannot refuse to pay them.
